record_metadata.scope: End-to-end explanation of how information moves across the global Internet.
record_metadata.primary_question: How does data move from one device or application to another across interconnected networks?
record_metadata.core_definition: The Internet is a global system of interconnected networks that communicate using standardized protocols, especially the Internet Protocol suite.
record_metadata.central_concept: The Internet is not one network owned or operated by one organization. It is a network of networks interconnected through routers, links, Internet service providers, peering relationships, transit providers, exchange points, data centers, and standardized protocols.

executive_model.one_sentence_explanation: Your device creates data, protocols divide and encapsulate that data into packets, local networking delivers the packets to a router, routers forward them across interconnected networks toward the destination, and the destination system reconstructs and processes the data.
simple_flow: DNS may translate a domain name into an IP address
Transport protocol establishes or manages communication
Data is divided into transport segments or datagrams
IP adds source and destination addressing
Link-layer technology places packets into local frames
Wi-Fi, Ethernet, cellular, fiber, or another access technology carries the frame
Local router forwards traffic toward an upstream network
Interconnected ISP networks exchange or transit the traffic
BGP helps networks determine reachable paths
Routers forward packets hop by hop
Backbone fiber or other long-distance infrastructure carries the traffic
Destination router forwards it toward the destination device
Response travels back through the network
executive_model.key_principle: No single router generally knows the entire physical journey of an individual packet. Each router primarily makes a forwarding decision based on its routing information and the packet's destination.

important_distinction.internet: The global network infrastructure and protocols.
important_distinction.web: One major application/service running on the Internet.
important_distinction.website: A collection of resources served through web protocols.
important_distinction.browser: Client software that communicates with web servers.
important_distinction.server: A computer or service providing resources or functions to clients.

what_the_internet_is.definition: A global interconnected system of independent and cooperating networks.

network_of_networks.meaning: Individual networks are interconnected so that devices on one network can communicate with devices and services on other networks.

end_to_end_example.scenario: A user opens a website in a browser.

step_01_user_action.event: User enters a domain name or selects a link.
step_01_user_action.result: The browser must determine how to reach the destination.

step_03_DNS_resolution.question: What IP address corresponds to the requested domain?
step_03_DNS_resolution.result: The browser or operating system obtains one or more destination IP addresses.

step_07_IP.purpose: Address the destination and provide routing across interconnected networks.

step_09_home_or_local_router.role: Forward traffic from the local network toward another network.

step_10_ISP.role: Provide connectivity from the user's network to other networks.

step_11_interprovider_routing.purpose: Exchange reachability information between autonomous systems.

step_14_server.role: Process the request and produce a response.

step_15_return_path.description: The response is transmitted back through the network using the applicable routing and transport mechanisms.

step_16_browser.role: Receives the response and renders the resulting resources.

physical_infrastructure.definition: The physical equipment and transmission systems carrying Internet traffic.

source_model.description: The Internet physically consists of routers and communications media such as cabling and radio links, while standardized protocols allow those heterogeneous systems to operate as an interconnected whole.
source_model.source_support: The supplied Internet article describes routers, media, repeaters, modems, heterogeneous hardware, and IP routing as components of Internet infrastructure.

packet_switching.definition: Data is transmitted through networks as packets rather than requiring a dedicated end-to-end physical circuit.
basic_process: Large data streams may be divided into smaller units
Packets are transmitted across network links
Each router selects an available next hop
Destination reconstructs or processes the received information
advantages: Ability to communicate with many destinations
packet_switching.historical_significance: Packet switching was one of the foundational concepts behind ARPANET and the modern Internet.
packet_switching.important_property: Different packets belonging to the same communication can potentially follow different paths.

protocol_stack.definition: The Internet uses multiple protocol layers, each responsible for a different aspect of communication.

layer_4_application.name: Application Layer
layer_4_application.purpose: Defines communication in terms appropriate to the application.

layer_2_internet.name: Internet Layer
layer_2_internet.purpose: Provides addressing and routing between networks.

layer_1_link.name: Link Layer
layer_1_link.purpose: Transfers frames across an individual local or physical network link.

encapsulation_model.transport_unit: TCP segment / UDP datagram / QUIC packet
encapsulation_model.physical_transmission: Bits/signals carried through the physical medium

encapsulation.definition: Each networking layer wraps the data from the layer above with information needed by the lower layer.

adds: Source MAC or equivalent link address

physical.result: Encoded electrical, optical, or radio signals

decapsulation.description: The destination removes the corresponding protocol layers and delivers the resulting payload to the appropriate application.

IP_addressing.purpose: Identify network interfaces and provide globally interoperable addressing for packet routing.

IPv4.address_space: Approximately 4.3 billion possible addresses before accounting for reserved and special-use ranges.

IPv6.purpose: Provide a vastly larger address space and modernized IP capabilities.

address_structure.network_prefix: Identifies the network or routing prefix.
address_structure.host_identifier: Identifies an interface or host within the applicable addressing structure.

CIDR.notation: Network address followed by slash and prefix length.
CIDR.meaning: The first 24 bits represent the network prefix.

private_vs_public.private_addresses: Used inside private networks and normally translated or otherwise mediated before reaching the public Internet.
private_vs_public.public_addresses: Globally routable address space used for Internet communication.

routing.definition: Routing is the process of determining where packets should be forwarded to reach their destinations.
basic_mechanism: Packet is transmitted through the selected interface

default_route.definition: A route used when no more-specific matching route exists.
default_route.common_example: Home device sends non-local traffic to its default gateway.

routing_scope.regional: Routing among networks within a provider or geographic region.
routing_scope.global: Routing among autonomous systems across the Internet.

typical_functions: Network address translation in applicable environments

important_distinction.switch: Primarily forwards frames within a local Layer 2 network.
important_distinction.modem: Converts or terminates signals appropriate to an access technology.

autonomous_systems.definition: A network or collection of networks under a common routing administration and policy.
autonomous_systems.global_role: Autonomous systems form major administrative and routing units of the Internet.

BGP.purpose: Exchange routing and reachability information between autonomous systems.
BGP.core_function: Allows independently operated networks to advertise which IP prefixes they can reach and to select paths according to routing policy.
BGP.important_concept: BGP is not simply a shortest-physical-distance algorithm. Routing decisions can reflect policy, commercial relationships, path attributes, redundancy, and other factors.
BGP.relationship_to_ISPs: ISPs and other autonomous systems use BGP to exchange reachability information.
BGP.relationship_to_global_Internet: BGP is a foundational protocol enabling the independently operated networks of the Internet to function as an interconnected global system.

ISP_hierarchy.definition: Internet connectivity is provided through networks operating at different scales and through different commercial and technical relationships.

tier_1.description: Large backbone networks with extensive global reach that can exchange traffic directly with one another.

tier_2.description: Networks that may peer with some networks while purchasing transit to reach other portions of the Internet.

lower_level_providers.description: Networks closer to end users that commonly purchase upstream transit and provide local access.

end_users.position: Edge of the global routing hierarchy

multihoming.definition: Connecting a network to more than one upstream provider.

peering.definition: Two networks directly exchange traffic for their respective networks or customers.

transit.definition: One network pays another network to provide connectivity to destinations beyond its own directly connected networks.
transit.purpose: Reach portions of the global Internet that are not directly accessible through the customer's own network or peering relationships.

relationship.peering: Direct exchange under an interconnection agreement.
relationship.transit: Purchased reachability through an upstream provider.

internet_exchange_points.purpose: Physical facilities where multiple networks interconnect and exchange traffic.

DNS.purpose: Translate human-readable domain names into network information such as IP addresses.
DNS.problem_solved: Humans generally use names while network protocols need addresses.

authoritative_servers.role: Provide authoritative DNS records for domains.

recursive_resolvers.role: Perform DNS lookups on behalf of clients and commonly cache results.

DNS.important_point: DNS does not carry the web page itself. It helps the client discover the network endpoint associated with a name.

ports_and_sockets.purpose: Identify application-level communication endpoints on hosts.
ports_and_sockets.IP_address: Identifies the network endpoint at the host/interface level.
ports_and_sockets.port: Identifies a transport-layer service or endpoint.

socket_model.concept: IP address plus transport protocol plus port identifies a communication endpoint.

TCP.purpose: Provide reliable ordered byte-stream communication between applications.
TCP.important_distinction: TCP reliability exists above IP. IP itself provides packet delivery across networks but does not by itself guarantee ordered, reliable application delivery.

QUIC.purpose: Modern secure transport supporting features useful for Internet applications.

HTTP.purpose: Transfer web resources and communicate between HTTP clients and servers.

components: TCP or QUIC depending on HTTP version

modern_examples.HTTP_1_1: Typically HTTP over TLS over TCP.
modern_examples.HTTP_2: Typically HTTP/2 over TLS over TCP.

certificate_model.server_certificate: Provides cryptographic identity information for the server.
certificate_model.certificate_authority: Trusted authority used to validate certificate chains.

basic_handshake_concept: Client and server negotiate supported cryptographic parameters
TLS.important_distinction: TLS protects the communication between endpoints but does not make the entire physical Internet path invisible to all network infrastructure. Network metadata such as IP addresses and traffic characteristics can still exist.

WiFi_and_Ethernet.relationship_to_IP: IP operates above these link technologies, allowing different local networking technologies to participate in the same global Internet.

cellular_internet.access_model: Mobile device connects through a cellular radio network.
cellular_internet.relationship_to_global_internet: The cellular carrier provides an access network that connects mobile devices into the broader Internet.

fiber_optics.role: Major high-capacity physical medium for Internet backbone and access networks.
advantages: Low attenuation compared with many older media

submarine_cables.role: Carry large volumes of international Internet traffic across oceans.

physical_structure.repeaters: Optical/electrical amplification or regeneration systems are used along long routes as applicable.
physical_structure.landing_stations: Connect submarine systems to terrestrial networks.

submarine_cables.important_point: The Internet is not primarily a collection of satellites. Modern international Internet traffic relies heavily on fiber-optic infrastructure, including submarine cables.

satellite_internet.role: Provide Internet connectivity through radio links involving satellites.
satellite_internet.relationship_to_historical_satnet: Modern satellite Internet continues the concept that satellite links can participate in packet-switched internetworking, while modern systems use technologies substantially different from early SATNET.

data_centers.definition: Facilities containing servers, storage systems, networking equipment, power systems, cooling systems, and physical security infrastructure.
data_centers.source_context: The supplied Internet article notes that most servers providing Internet services are hosted in data centers and that colocation facilities commonly host peering, transit, cloud, exchange-point, and submarine-cable connectivity.

cloud_computing.definition: Large-scale distributed computing infrastructure exposed as services over networks.
cloud_computing.relationship_to_internet: Cloud infrastructure provides many of the servers and services users access through the Internet.
cloud_computing.important_distinction: Cloud computing is not synonymous with the Internet. Cloud services run on infrastructure that is connected to the Internet.

content_delivery_networks.purpose: Distribute content from geographically distributed edge locations closer to users.

servers.definition: Systems that provide computational resources, data, or services to other systems.

modern_architecture.microservices: Application functionality divided into multiple services.
modern_architecture.cloud: Infrastructure dynamically provisioned across large facilities.

load_balancing.purpose: Distribute requests or connections across multiple servers or service instances.

anycast.concept: The same IP address or service prefix can be announced from multiple geographically distributed locations.
anycast.routing_behavior: Network routing directs a client toward one of the available instances according to routing and policy.
anycast.benefit: Provides geographic distribution and resilience without requiring clients to know the physical location of every service instance.

NAT.purpose: Translate between address spaces, commonly private internal addresses and public Internet addresses.
typical_process: NAT gateway changes source address and often source port
Internet receives traffic using the gateway's public address
Response traffic is translated back toward the internal device
NAT.important_point: NAT is not the same thing as a firewall, although consumer gateways commonly implement both.

DHCP.purpose: Automatically provide network configuration to devices.

IPv4.purpose: Resolve an IPv4 address to a local link-layer address.

IPv6.purpose: Provide IPv6 neighbor and local-link discovery functions.

ARP_and_neighbor_discovery.importance: These mechanisms connect IP-layer addressing to local-link delivery.

firewall.purpose: Control traffic according to security policy.

firewalls_and_network_security.important_point: Internet security is not one mechanism. It is a layered system of controls.

standards_model.RFC: Request for Comments documents define many Internet protocols, standards, experimental technologies, and informational documents.

ICANN.full_name: Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers
role: Coordinates IP addressing parameters through the broader Internet number-management system

RIRs.purpose: Regional allocation and management of Internet number resources.

Internet_Society.role: Supports the open development, evolution, and use of the Internet.

IETF.role: Develops and maintains many Internet standards and protocols.

IAB.role: Provides architectural oversight and guidance within the Internet standards ecosystem.

internet_governance_and_standards.important_principle: The Internet is decentralized operationally, while shared standards and registries provide the interoperability necessary for independent networks to communicate.

1974.event: Cerf and Kahn published their packet-network intercommunication proposal.

1977.event: ARPANET, SATNET, and PRNET interconnected in a major internetworking demonstration.

1983.event: TCP/IP became the production protocol architecture of ARPANET.

1986.event: NSFNET expanded network access to supercomputing and research sites.

1989.event: Commercial Internet service providers emerged in the United States and Australia.

major_developments: Rapid growth of public Internet access

world_wide_web.relationship_to_internet: The Web is an application/service running on top of the Internet, not the Internet itself.

internet_services.principle: The Internet provides the underlying connectivity; applications use protocols and services layered above it.

email.important_point: Email is an Internet application that uses multiple application and transport protocols.

creation.description: An application generates information that needs to be transmitted.

encapsulation.description: Protocol layers add addressing, transport, and link information.

local_transmission.description: The device sends a frame onto the local network.

gateway.description: The local router receives the frame and forwards the IP packet toward another network.

routing.description: Each router selects a next hop using forwarding information.

backbone_transport.description: Packets cross one or more provider and backbone networks.

destination_network.description: The packet reaches the network containing the destination service.

final_delivery.description: Routers and local networking deliver the packet to the destination host.

decapsulation.description: The destination protocol stack removes the network wrappers.

application_processing.description: The application receives and processes the payload.

response.description: A response follows the applicable reverse communication path.

generally_preserved_end_to_end: Encrypted payload when protected by TLS
what_can_change_along_the_path.important_point: The Internet is layered specifically so that different underlying networks can carry the same higher-level communication.

latency.definition: Time required for information to travel through the network and for processing to occur.
latency.important_point: Higher bandwidth does not automatically mean lower latency.

bandwidth.definition: The capacity of a link or network path to carry data.

congestion.definition: A condition in which offered traffic approaches or exceeds available network capacity.

control.network: Routers and providers may use queue management and traffic engineering.

redundancy_and_resilience.principle: The Internet can often route around failures because it consists of interconnected networks with multiple possible paths.
redundancy_and_resilience.historical_lineage: Distributed routing and network survivability were important themes in the development of packet-switched networking.
redundancy_and_resilience.important_distinction: Resilience does not mean the Internet cannot fail. Large-scale outages can occur when multiple critical systems or paths fail simultaneously.

security_model.important_principle: The Internet protocol stack provides connectivity, but security must be implemented across multiple layers.

global_internet_topology.topology_principle: The global Internet is a distributed graph of independently operated networks connected through many physical and logical relationships.

logical_graph.BGP: Provides inter-domain reachability information and policy.

physical_graph.description: Actual cables, radio links, routers, switches, facilities, and transmission equipment.

application_graph.description: Applications create logical relationships between services and clients that may span many physical networks.

internet.definition: Global interconnected network infrastructure and protocols.

world_wide_web.definition: A distributed information and application system using Internet connectivity, primarily through HTTP/HTTPS.

cloud.definition: Large-scale computing infrastructure and services delivered through networks.

data_center.definition: Physical facility containing computing and networking infrastructure.

website.definition: A collection of web resources delivered by one or more servers/services.

browser.definition: Client application used to interact with web resources.

identity_and_name.function: Resolve service name to network destination.

response.path: Destination back toward client through the applicable network stack.

top_to_bottom: HTTP / DNS / SMTP / SSH / other application protocols
Ethernet / Wi-Fi / Cellular / other link technologies

SATNET.role: Early packet satellite network and heterogeneous internetworking platform.

PRNET.role: Radio-based packet network used in early internetworking experiments.

TCP_IP.role: Provided the protocol foundation for interconnecting heterogeneous networks.

NSFNET.role: Major research and academic network that helped expand Internet connectivity.

World_Wide_Web.creator: Tim Berners-Lee
World_Wide_Web.role: Made Internet-based information access dramatically more accessible through linked documents and browsers.

internet_is_the_web.correction: The Web is one service running on the Internet.

internet_is_one_network.correction: The Internet is a network of interconnected networks.

DNS_carries_web_pages.correction: DNS primarily provides name-resolution information; HTTP/HTTPS carries web application data.

routers_store_the_whole_internet.correction: Routers use routing and forwarding information appropriate to their scope; they do not need a complete map of every physical link.

TCP_is_the_internet.correction: TCP is one transport protocol within the larger Internet protocol suite.

IP_guarantees_delivery.correction: IP provides packet delivery and routing semantics but does not itself guarantee reliable ordered delivery.

satellites_carry_most_international_inte.correction: Modern international Internet connectivity relies heavily on fiber-optic infrastructure, especially submarine cables.

cloud_is_the_internet.correction: Cloud services run on computing infrastructure connected through networks, including the Internet.

one_company_controls_the_internet.correction: The Internet consists of independently operated networks using shared protocols, standards, registries, and interconnection arrangements.

ARPANET.role: Major predecessor to the modern Internet

operational_roles.local_router: Connects the local network to upstream networks.
operational_roles.regional_network: Aggregates and transports traffic across a geographic region.
operational_roles.peer: Directly exchanges traffic with another network.
operational_roles.backbone: Carries high volumes of long-distance traffic.
operational_roles.CDN: Caches and serves content from distributed locations.
operational_roles.browser: Consumes web resources and renders them for users.

layer_2_local_network: Does the device have a local IP?
layer_3_IP: Can the destination IP be reached?
layer_4_transport: Is TCP or QUIC establishing correctly?
layer_7_HTTP: Does the server return a response?
Is the application returning an error?

mail_system.analogy: The Internet can be partially understood as a highly automated global mail system.
mail_system.limitation: The analogy is useful for intuition but does not represent the actual technical implementation.

architectural_principles.encapsulation: Each layer adds information needed for its operation.
architectural_principles.interoperability: Independent systems communicate through shared protocols.
architectural_principles.decentralization: No single machine carries all Internet traffic.
architectural_principles.distributed_control: Many independent organizations operate portions of the infrastructure.
architectural_principles.packet_switching: Network capacity is shared among many communications.
architectural_principles.routing: Traffic can be forwarded across multiple interconnected networks.
architectural_principles.redundancy: Multiple paths and systems can improve resilience.
architectural_principles.end_to_end_communication: Applications communicate across many intermediate networks without requiring every intermediate network to understand application semantics.
architectural_principles.scalability: Hierarchical addressing, routing, naming, and distributed infrastructure allow the system to grow.

trace.action: Resolve example.com to an IP address.
Send traffic through Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
Forward packet outside the local network.
Select next network based on routing information.
Move traffic between independently operated networks.
Receive traffic for the destination prefix.
Decrypt, parse, execute, and render the response.

supplied_source_topics: Internet as a network of networks

source_caveats.scope: This schema expands the supplied Internet article into a technical explanatory model.
source_caveats.historical_vs_modern: Historical networking technologies such as ARPANET, SATNET, NPL, and PRNET should not be interpreted as identical to modern Internet infrastructure.
source_caveats.layer_model: The four-layer Internet protocol suite is a conceptual model. Real implementations can have additional sublayers and technologies.
source_caveats.routing: Actual Internet routing is substantially more complex than the simplified hop-by-hop model presented here.
source_caveats.BGP: BGP provides inter-domain reachability and policy mechanisms; it should not be reduced to a simple shortest-path algorithm.
source_caveats.DNS: DNS can return more than a single IP address, and modern DNS deployments can include caching, load balancing, geographic steering, security extensions, and other mechanisms.
source_caveats.HTTP: Modern web applications may use HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, or HTTP/3, with HTTP/3 using QUIC.
source_caveats.security: TLS, firewalls, authentication, endpoint security, routing security, and physical controls operate at different layers and solve different problems.
source_caveats.physical_infrastructure: The schema describes the major infrastructure categories rather than an exhaustive inventory of global cables, routers, facilities, providers, or data centers.
source_caveats.cloud_and_CDN: Cloud and CDN architectures vary substantially between providers and applications.
source_caveats.modern_operations: Actual production networks may use SDN, network virtualization, service meshes, overlays, EVPN, MPLS, SR-MPLS, SRv6, programmable switches, distributed load balancing, and other technologies not exhaustively represented here.

machine_readable_summary.definition: Global interconnected network of independently operated networks using standardized protocols.
